headline: This 2022 law lets the Supreme Court's Marshal and Supreme Court Police protect certain family members of justices and Court officers when the Marshal finds it necessary.
what_it_does: The law gives the Marshal of the Supreme Court and the Supreme Court Police the authority to protect members of the immediate family of the Chief Justice and Associate Justices. It also covers any officer of the Supreme Court. Protection applies only when the Marshal decides it is necessary.

who_it_affects.group: The Marshal of the Supreme Court and Supreme Court Police
who_it_affects.how: They gain explicit authority to provide protection to specified family members and officers when the Marshal decides it is needed.

who_it_affects.group: Immediate family members of the Chief Justice and Associate Justices
who_it_affects.how: They may receive security protection from the Supreme Court Police if the Marshal determines it is necessary.
They may receive security protection from the Supreme Court Police if the Marshal determines it is necessary.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on June 16, 2022, and the official summary does not list a separate later effective date.
